title: Generic Committed-State Restore, Persistence Boundary & Provenance Qualification

source_bound_problem.missing_capability: safe reconstruction of an already-advanced committed revision

excluded_contents: reporting history that is not continuation state
selected_contract.construction: only an already-ready kernel_committed_state_t may export the opaque carrier
selected_contract.restore: only an uninitialized kernel_committed_state_t may restore from a ready carrier after schema and expected-layout validation

lineage_decision.policy: preserve stable lineage id across committed-boundary restart
lineage_decision.reason: existing checkpoint, candidate and accepted-window provenance bind to lineage plus revision; no generic safe provenance-rebind protocol exists, so lineage rotation would invalidate dependent carriers or require owner-specific rewriting

versioning.layout_id: positive runtime/template identity supplied at export and required exactly at restore
versioning.note: layout identity is persistence provenance, not immutable parameter duplication and not solver scratch

integrity_boundary.security_claim: logical API integrity, not cryptographic authenticity
integrity_boundary.serialization_note: a later trusted adapter may serialize a versioned representation; F-KT12 does not define byte-level import or a user-facing restart format

required_semantics: restored physical state equals exported committed physical state
next checkpoint starts from restored revision and time
next candidate origin revision equals restored revision
commit continues monotonically at restored revision plus one
restore itself creates no physical transfer and no water-ledger reset
request, forcing and parameter objects remain nonmutated

negative_cases: restore into already initialized committed state

architecture_invariants.16_multiswap_primary: compatible with per-column compact carrier and external template/layout identity
